notes:
- **The answer turns up as it is written**, a line at a time, instead of arriving all at once when
  your agent has finished thinking. This is in the Archie window, on an Anthropic account of your
  own. On the other AI companies, and in Slack, Telegram and the rest, the answer still comes in one
  piece.
- **Your agent writes a real PDF.** Typeset on this computer, with numbered pages, and if the answer
  had a chart in it the chart is drawn into the page rather than listed. Ask for slides and you get
  a deck with one heading per slide. The deck opens in Keynote. Nobody here has been able to open it
  in PowerPoint yet, so it does not promise that until somebody has.
- **It can read a PDF that is a photograph of a page.** Some PDFs are pictures of paper, with no
  words in the file at all, and Archie used to say so and stop. Tick **Read PDFs that are scans**,
  under Setup, and it looks at the pages instead: up to ten of them, when you ask it to open the
  file and there was nothing to read. It costs a cent or two each time, on your own AI account, and
  it needs an Anthropic key. With any other AI company the box does nothing and the screen says so.
- **Paste in an AI key and Archie opens, free.** No plan, no trial running out. You get 20 jobs a
  day, five of them held back for things you ask for yourself, so a routine cannot spend the lot
  before you wake up. The count starts again at midnight. This is Archie; Archie for Business still
  takes a plan.
- **You can switch off things your agent can do.** Under Setup, What it can do, there is one switch
  for each: building skills, adding and removing add-ons, running routines, setting reminders,
  reading its own record, saving files, changing its own AI settings, and going to the web. All of
  them start on. Turning one off stops your agent offering it, and the row says where to turn it
  back on.
- **Your agent keeps what it used to forget, and you can tell it a fact yourself.** What it
  remembered was trimmed oldest first, so something you mentioned once in March was gone by
  September with nowhere to look it up. What gets dropped now goes to an archive beside it and comes
  back on its own when something you say touches it. The Memory panel takes typing now too: write a
  fact in, or correct one it got wrong.
- **Two tabs have better names.** Now is called **Dashboard** and Work is called **Jobs**. The
  messages your agent sends you say the new names too.
- **Connecting Gmail asks Google for one permission instead of three.** It was always one
  permission; the consent screen just described it three times, which read as three.
- **Replies start about a second sooner.** Every message waited 1.2 seconds before any work began,
  holding the door open for a second message that in most cases was never coming. The wait is a
  quarter of a second now, and the full wait comes straight back the moment a second message proves
  you are still typing.
- **Every service in the store carries its own mark**, and you can narrow the store to one app you
  have connected and see only what works with it. Five marks came off because the companies that own
  them say we may not draw them; those rows say the company's name instead.
- **Archie for Business has its own icon**, in the dock, in the window and on the download.
- **Archie has a trademarks screen**, naming the companies whose marks appear in the app and saying
  the marks belong to them.
- **New in the store:** My Classes, Class Planner, Leave Time and Flight Check-In, with routines to
  go with them: The Week in Classes, Due Soon, The School's Own Dates, The Morning Drive Check, The
  Traffic Watch and Check-In Window. There is a **College** pack that puts the class ones together.
  The old Student pack is now called **Self-Study**, which is what it always was; nothing in it
  changed.
- Ember has a back now, four more things it does between answers, and a backflip.
- The box you type in grows with what you are writing instead of scrolling inside four lines.
- Paste a new key straight over a connected app, instead of disconnecting it first and starting
  again.
- A routine you have switched off now looks switched off. The only sign used to be a small pill at
  the end of its name, with the line underneath still reading "weekdays at 7:00 am".
- **Fixed: ask about one mailbox and your agent reads that mailbox.** The list it worked from was
  capped at ten messages across every address you have connected, and the cut was by how recent
  they were, so one busy address could take the whole list and the address you asked about
  contribute nothing to it. Each one is guaranteed a share now, and your agent can tell you there
  is more to see.
- Fixed: the browser window your agent opens now closes whichever way the job ends, and Archie comes
  back to the front when it hands something over to you.
